title: The Lantern Pulley Puzzle
markdown:
The Science Club had a colourful problem. Their party was coming, and they wanted sparkly lanterns hung super high in the hall. Way, way up there, where the rafters kept their secrets.

Iris, who always looked like a happy little question mark, bounced on her toes. “They need to go up there!” She pointed at the ceiling.

Button the badger, sturdy and ready, nodded. “Right then. Let’s get lifting.”

Iris grabbed one end of a lantern string, Button the other. Professor Elm cheered, “Heave ho!”

WHOOSH — it was way harder than they thought. Iris’s arms wobbled like jelly. Button’s strong legs braced. The lantern swayed, barely moving. Like trying to lift a whole cloud over their heads. Their shoulders complained. The lantern did not.

“Oh dear,” puffed Elm. “Too high for a simple lift. Our arms aren’t long enough.” The unhung lanterns drooped a little sadly.

Iris’s thinking brain spun. Through the open door she saw a crow pulling on a long vine to reach berries on a high branch. The crow did not fly up with the berries. It pulled from where it stood, and the vine did the travelling.

“Look! That crow. The vine helps it get the berries.”

Elm peered out. “A helper for our lanterns?”

Iris dinged again. “We have rope. And that strong branch above the door. What if we looped the rope over it? Like a slide for the rope.”

Button scurried off and returned with thick sturdy rope. They looped it over the branch, hanging down on both sides. One end waited. The other end waited. The branch was not a magic wheel. It was a smooth place for the rope to turn.

“I’ll tie one end to the lantern. Button, you grab the other end down here. You can pull down instead of lifting up.”

Button grabbed the loose end, hanging low. Iris secured the lantern to the other.

“Ready?” Iris whispered.

“Ready!” puffed Button.

He pulled down. To their amazement, the lantern on the other side of the branch rose slowly, steadily, safely. It just went up. Pulling down used Button’s weight; lifting over their heads had been all arms. The lantern was still a lantern. It had not become a feather. The job had simply changed direction.

“It’s working!”

Button grinned. “Pulling this way is so much easier than lifting!”

Soon all the beautiful lanterns hung high and bright, ready for the party. The hall smelled of polish and paper lanterns. Button sat down, pleased, and did not pretend he had lifted a cloud with one paw.

Elm clapped. “What you and Button have created is called a pulley.”

Iris blinked. “A pulley?”

“A helper rope over a wheel — or, tonight, a branch. Pull down on one end, the other goes up. You change the direction of the pull. That’s why it felt kinder than heaving the lantern skyward. You could lean into it.”

Button wiggled his nose. “We were pulling down to make them go up.”

“Exactly. A simple machine. Direction, and a pull you can lean into.”

Iris looked at the lanterns, the rope, the branch. “A pulley. I wonder what else we can lift.”

The hall filled with light. Cozy as a clubroom should be. Iris wondered what other helpers might be hiding in plain rope, and Button, who liked a job you could pull, already had his eye on a banner that wanted to go just a little higher.
characters: Iris (a puzzle solver), Button (a badger), Elm (a professor)
author: StoryGen Community
